column2: The Coastal Treaty: Delivery of the Territories

Peace has been concluded, but a treaty is more than a signature on paper. The districts of Natal and Zululand promised to the South African Republic must pass into republican administration, together with the lands of Mabhudu. British officers are to surrender the agreed posts, and the commandants will arrange the handover of public offices, roads and frontier stations. The terms bind the imperial authorities and the local administrations alike. An intervening change of governor or the disappearance of a dependent state cannot cancel the agreement. The Volksraad records these districts as territory of the republic, while the Cape remains outside this limited settlement. Let the maps and registers now reflect the peace we accepted.
Carry out the treaty: these lands belong to the republic.
